title: Identification of fungal enzymes involving 3-phenoxybenzoic acid degradation by using enzymes inhibitors and inducers
author: Zhao, Chen, et al.

steps.title: Prepare induced and control cultures
steps.instruction: Culture Aspergillus oryzae M‑4 in medium containing 0.24 mM 3‑PBA and its intermediate metabolites (induced sample) and in identical medium without any additives (non‑inducible control). Incubate replicates at 30 °C, 180 rpm for 24, 36, 48, 60 and 72 h. Measure fungal biomass as described by Zhao et al. (2019). At 48 h the strain is in logarithmic growth; use cultures harvested at this time for subsequent experiments.

substeps.instruction: Prepare two media: one with 0.24 mM 3‑PBA + intermediates, one without additives.
Inoculate each medium with the degrading strain.
Incubate at 30 °C, 180 rpm for the specified durations.
Measure biomass according to Zhao et al. (2019).
Select the 48 h cultures (log phase) for further work.

steps.title: Harvest mycelia and prepare cell extracts
steps.instruction: Filter 30 mL of the 48 h culture through a paper filter to collect mycelial pellets and filter liquor. Wash the pellets 1–5 times with sterile water, measuring 3‑PBA and metabolite concentrations after each wash; after the second wash concentrations are essentially zero. Resuspend the washed pellets in 30 mL phosphate buffer (50 mM, pH 7.0). Disrupt the resuspended pellets by ultrasonication (method of Fang et al., 2015) to obtain a cell‑debris solution.

substeps.instruction: Filter the culture and separate mycelial pellets from filter liquor.
Wash pellets 1–5 times, checking substrate levels after each wash.
After two washes, confirm near‑zero substrate concentration.
Resuspend pellets in 30 mL 50 mM phosphate buffer, pH 7.0.
Ultrasonicate the suspension to produce a cell‑debris solution.

steps.title: Conduct substrate degradation assays
steps.instruction: Mix equal volumes of the filter‑liquor solution and the cell‑debris solution with phosphate buffer containing 0.048 mM each of 3‑PBA and its intermediate metabolites. Incubate the reaction mixtures at 30 °C, 180 rpm for 24, 48 or 72 h. Terminate each reaction by adding an equal volume of acetonitrile. Quantify residual 3‑PBA and metabolites by HPLC and calculate degradation using Eq. (1).

substeps.instruction: Prepare reaction mixtures with equal parts filter liquor, cell debris, and phosphate buffer (0.048 mM each substrate).
Incubate at 30 °C, 180 rpm for the chosen duration (24, 48, or 72 h).
Stop the reaction by adding the same volume of acetonitrile.
Analyze samples by HPLC and compute degradation percentage.

steps.title: Time‑course degradation and enzyme activity assays
steps.instruction: Add 1.5 mL of the degrading‑strain inoculum to a 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask containing 30 mL medium with 0.24 mM 3‑PBA. Incubate at 30 °C, 180 rpm for 24, 48, 72 and 96 h. Identify the time point showing the greatest change in substrate/metabolite concentrations. Filter that culture, collect mycelial pellets and filter liquor, and assay the activities of cytochrome P450 (CYP450), lignin peroxidase (LiP), laccase, manganese peroxidase (MnP) and dioxygenase using the referenced methods (Refs [15], [9], [16]).

substeps.instruction: Inoculate flasks with 1.5 mL inoculum and 30 mL medium containing 0.24 mM 3‑PBA.
Incubate at 30 °C, 180 rpm for 24, 48, 72, and 96 h.
Measure substrate and metabolite concentrations at each time point.
Select the sample with the largest concentration shift.
Filter the selected culture and collect pellets and liquor.
Determine enzyme activities (CYP450, LiP, laccase, MnP, dioxygenase) as described in the cited protocols.

steps.title: Test inhibitors and inducers effects
steps.instruction: Prepare inhibitor/inducer solutions: dissolve CuSO₄, NaN₃ and AgNO₃ in water; dissolve piperonyl‑butoxide (PBO) in ethanol; dissolve EDTA in 10 % (w/v) NaOH. In five 250 mL flasks each containing 30 mL MD medium with 0.24 mM 3‑PBA or an intermediate metabolite, add filter‑sterilized volumes of ethyl alcohol, CuSO₄, NaN₃, AgNO₃ or PBO to obtain final concentrations of 0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 5.0 and 10.0 × 0.24 mM, respectively. Add 1.5 mL of strain M‑4 inoculum and incubate at 30 °C, 180 rpm for 72 h. After incubation, determine substrate and metabolite concentrations by HPLC, calculate degradation (Eq. 1), and measure dry‑weight biomass (g L⁻¹) as described by Zhao et al. (2019). Analyze the relationship between degradation and each inhibitor/inducer to infer enzyme involvement.

substeps.instruction: Prepare stock solutions: CuSO₄, NaN₃, AgNO₃ in water; PBO in ethanol; EDTA in 10 % NaOH.
Set up five 250 mL flasks with 30 mL MD medium containing 0.24 mM 3‑PBA or an intermediate.
Add filter‑sterilized inhibitor/inducer solutions to achieve final concentrations of 0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 5.0 and 10.0 × 0.24 mM, respectively.
Inoculate each flask with 1.5 mL of the degrading‑strain culture.
Incubate at 30 °C, 180 rpm for 72 h.
Measure residual substrates by HPLC, calculate degradation, and determine dry‑weight biomass (g L⁻¹).
Interpret how each inhibitor/inducer affects degradation to identify involved enzymes.
